column1: # The measured proof-check time and memory of each unit with proofs, for `oft plan`'s packing of check jobs: its
# minutes and its peak memory in GiB (the longest and the largest of its whole-job runs on the release gate, one
# n2-highmem-32, 32 vCPU, per unit), and `cpus`, the CPUs its check job may give dune on a
# 16-core 64 GB runner, from outcomes measured there: the column's largest value, 16, is every CPU the runner has
# (so a larger runner is not held to 16), and fewer only where a check at 16 ran out of memory or swapped. A unit
# not listed counts as the median of the listed minutes and gets every CPU. The minutes and the peaks are the gate's
# 32-vCPU numbers; `oft check` prints a `peak memory` line per unit on the runner that ran it, from which the `cpus`
# column is judged. The table decides only how units are packed into jobs and their CPUs, never what is checked.
